affected_system: municipal capital planning, debt, grants, reserves, procurement, and asset delivery
alternatives: protect minimum coverage before needs-based allocation of municipal capital funding and delivery capacity
adapt allocations using observed demand, uptake, and capacity for municipal capital funding and delivery capacity
pair legal, fiscal, dependency, readiness, and minimum-service allocation with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Budgets, obligations, appropriations, encumbrances, expenditures, schedules, and assets are reconciled.
All fiscal scenarios separate nominal, real, committed, contingent, and modeled amounts.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: retain the current distribution rule for municipal capital funding and delivery capacity.

constraints.description: The capital portfolio and municipal finance allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: chief financial officer and capital planning director
decision_question: How should pay-as-you-go funds, debt, grants, reserves, and project staff be assigned?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The capital portfolio and municipal finance allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
independence_key.decision_object: municipal capital funding and delivery capacity
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for municipal capital funding and delivery capacity passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: legal, fiscal, dependency, readiness, and minimum-service allocation
independence_key.primary_outcome: priority capital need without assigned affordable capacity

intended_claim: A versioned allocate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting municipal capital funding and delivery capacity, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: priority capital need without assigned affordable capacity
distributional gap in priority capital need without assigned affordable capacity
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not report a modeled allocation as an appropriation, bond issuance, grant, or expenditure.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for municipal capital funding and delivery capacity passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.

title: Allocate capital funding and delivery capacity
transportability_risks: Accounting, tax authority, debt limits, grants, procurement, labor, and markets differ.
Historical delivery and cost relationships may shift under inflation or policy change.
